rfi.title: 'My home wasn't safe anymore': lessons from France's hottest summer yet
rfi.description: It was France's most severe heatwave on record: almost 8,000 excess deaths, some 120,000 hectares of scorched land, livestock and crops lost, birds falling silent in blackened forests. And for Juliette Decq, a climate consultant and mother of two, it was also the summer her home stopped feeling safe.

rfi.title: Nigeria names panel to probe deaths of 37 miners held in detention
rfi.description: Nigeria's government has appointed a 10-member independent panel to investigate the deaths of 37 people while they were held in custody on suspicion of illegal gold-mining in Niger state.

rfi.title: Congolese cyclist dies in crash during 'Pedals for Peace' journey
rfi.description: Miguel Masaisai, a Congolese cyclist who set out to promote peace by riding from his home city of Goma to Morocco, has died in a road accident in the northern Republic of the Congo.

rfi.title: Denmark welcomes deal with US over Greenland after Trump annexation threats
rfi.description: Denmark's government has welcomed a US deal on Greenland to bolster US military presence there while keeping the island under Danish control, following months of threats by President Donald Trump to seize the semi-autonomous territory of a NATO ally.

rfi.title: Europe weighs the cost of sending its own astronauts into space
rfi.description: French President Emmanuel Macron wants Europe to develop its own way of sending astronauts into space within a decade. Europe already builds rockets and satellites and sends astronauts to the International Space Station – but it still relies on American spacecraft to get them there. As the global space sector expands, the question is whether Europe should invest in closing that gap, and what it would take to do so.

rfi.title: France calls on Moscow to reverse takeover of European assets
rfi.description: France has called on Moscow to "reverse" its decision to take control of assets belonging to European companies still operating in Russia, including Swiss food giant Nestle and three French groups. The Kremlin defends the takeover as a justified measure against firms representing "unfriendly countries" that back Ukraine.

rfi.title: As far right gains ground in Germany, Berlin election tests Europe's centre
rfi.description: Berliners go to the polls on Sunday to elect the city-state’s parliament and district councils, in a vote taking place just two weeks after the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) secured a historic victory in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt. The implications could extend beyond Germany.

rfi.title: Tiny French outpost off Canada the unlikely stage for new transatlantic courtship
rfi.description: A tiny piece of France just off Canada’s Atlantic coast will become the setting for a much bigger geopolitical story on Sunday, when President Emmanuel Macron welcomes Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney to Saint-Pierre and Miquelon. The meeting brings Canada’s push for closer ties with Europe to a territory that has long sat at the crossroads of French, Canadian and US interests in the North Atlantic.

rfi.title: Sweeping raids leave Turkey’s LGBTQI+ community fearing what comes next
rfi.description: Turkey has jailed dozens of people pending trial as a sweeping crackdown on LGBTQI+ groups widens, prompting international condemnation and protests outside Turkish embassies on Friday.

rfi.title: Russians vote for new parliament after campaign marked by near silence
rfi.description: Russians began voting on Friday in three days of parliamentary elections to choose the 450 members of the State Duma, after a campaign with little public debate or television coverage. More than four years into the war in Ukraine, candidates have also had few opportunities to challenge Kremlin policies.

rfi.title: Locked in Arctic ice, the floating lab studying climate and wildlife
rfi.description: A floating laboratory has begun drifting through Arctic sea ice on a mission set to last until late 2027, carrying scientists into one of the most isolated places on Earth. Built in France, the Tara Polar Station is carrying a crew of 12 to study biodiversity and the effects of climate change, as well as a dog to alert them to polar bears – and no one knows exactly where the ice will take them.

rfi.title: French police officer detained over terror plot linked to far-right ideology
rfi.description: A French police officer suspected of adhering to violent far-right ideology has been arrested and placed in pre-trial detention over an alleged plot to carry out terrorist attacks, according to judicial sources.

rfi.title: French prosecutors investigate sexual harassment involving smart glasses
rfi.description: French prosecutors have opened a criminal investigation into suspected sexual harassment involving smart glasses, after complaints about women being filmed in the street without their knowledge and the footage being posted online.

rfi.title: Nestlé to face retrial over illegal dumping near French bottled water plants
rfi.description: Nestlé Waters is to face a new trial over alleged illegal dumping near its bottled water plants in eastern France, after an appeals court reinstated key scientific evidence excluded from the original proceedings.

rfi.title: A city at the crossroads of history: Unearthing Gaza's ancient heritage
rfi.description: Before Gaza became synonymous with conflict, it was a place where merchants sold wine from local vineyards, pilgrims crossed continents, fishermen set out before dawn, and generations of families lived between sea and desert. RFI explores its deep history.

rfi.title: Canada and EU 'stronger together' says Carney, brushing aside US threats
rfi.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney on Thursday welcomed a proposal for his country to become the European Union's first "associate member", shrugging off threats from United States President Donald Trump.

rfi.title: From Peru to the Philippines, defending the land comes at a deadly cost
rfi.description: People defending their land, forests and communities continue to face killings, arrests and intimidation around the world – with Latin America by far the most dangerous region, the environmental campaign group Global Witness has found. In the Philippines, one community resisting a mining project has told RFI of arrests, injuries and legal action against residents trying to stop work on their land.

lemonde.title: En Asie, l’imprévisibilité de Donald Trump pousse ses alliés à repenser leur sécurité
lemonde.description: La politique ambiguë du président américain dans la région a ravivé les doutes sur la fiabilité des Etats-Unis en cas de conflit avec la Chine. Face aux ambitions régionales de Pékin, partenaires et alliés historiques de Washington resserrent leurs liens et musclent leurs capacités de défense.

lemonde.title: En Allemagne, Friedrich Merz joue sa survie politique lors des élections régionales de dimanche

lemonde.title: Emma Heming Willis sur la maladie de son mari, Bruce Willis : « Malgré l’incapacité à communiquer, l’amour est là, je sais que je vivrai la suite de l’histoire avec lui »
lemonde.description: A 67 ans, l’acteur américain apprenait souffrir de dégénérescence fronto-temporale. Près de quatre ans après le diagnostic, son épouse raconte comment elle a composé avec la maladie et son nouveau rôle d’aidante. Un récit qu’elle livre également dans un ouvrage, traduit en français au printemps.

lemonde.title: « Mon dossier s’était perdu dans les limbes de la CAF » : le grand saut administratif vers l’âge adulte
lemonde.description: Bourses, Assurance-maladie, impôts… Les jeunes découvrent un nouveau parcours du combattant : celui de la paperasse, entre formulaires et plateformes numériques, et passent souvent à côté d’aides auxquelles ils auraient pu être éligibles.

lemonde.title: Catherine Ringer, célèbre voix des Rita Mitsouko, inhumée à Paris aux côtés de Fred Chichin
lemonde.description: La chanteuse, morte lundi des suites d’un cancer à l’âge de 68 ans, avait souhaité des obsèques dans la plus stricte intimité.

lemonde.title: « L’enquête PISA nous rappelle que nous ne sommes plus capables d’établir ce que nous voulons en priorité pour notre école »
lemonde.description: Le sociologue et chercheur en sciences de l’éducation Xavier Pons décrypte, dans une tribune au « Monde », l’évolution du débat public sur les résultats du Programme international de suivi des acquis des élèves de 15 ans, et invite à réfléchir à de nouveaux outils pour améliorer « la fabrique des réformes scolaires ».

lemonde.title: Budget 2027 : le pas de deux entre Sébastien Lecornu et le Rassemblement national

lemonde.title: Pourquoi sommes-nous si mal assis dans les lieux branchés ?
lemonde.description: Dans les adresses les plus courues de Paris, s’asseoir est devenu un sport de combat : tabourets minuscules, terrasses bondées où l’on finit debout, voire assis à même le trottoir. Cet inconfort est de plus en plus assumé par les restaurateurs comme par une clientèle prête à souffrir un peu pour être au bon endroit. Enquête sur cette discrète guerre des sièges.

lemonde.title: Au Festival du « Monde », une rédaction mobilisée face au défi d’une présidentielle sous tension : « La communication étouffe la politique »
lemonde.description: Au Festival du « Monde », samedi 19 septembre, Mariama Darame, journaliste au service politique du quotidien, évoquait, lors d’une rencontre avec les lecteurs, les enjeux de la couverture de la campagne présidentielle.

lemonde.title: L’Olympique lyonnais et le Paris FC prennent place sur le podium de Ligue 1
lemonde.description: L’OL a surclassé Rennes (4-0) en lui infligeant sa première défaite de la saison en championnat, lors de la 5e journée, samedi. Le PFC a, lui, dominé Strasbourg (2-1) et confirmé ses ambitions. Le Mans et Toulouse ont signé leur première victoire.

france24fr.title: En direct : dernier jour des élections législatives en Russie
france24fr.description: Les Russes se rendent aux urnes dimanche pour le troisième et dernier jour d'élections législatives, les premières depuis le début de l'offensive à grande échelle contre l'Ukraine en 2022. Ces législatives qui se déroulent aussi dans les territoires d'Ukraine occupés et annexés par la Russie devraient sans surprise se solder par la victoire du parti de Vladimir Poutine. Suivez notre direct.

france24fr.title: Trump va nommer un "tsar" pour "chérir, aider et veiller sur" l'IA
france24fr.description: Le président américain a affirmé samedi qu'il n'accepterait rien qui puisse faire obstacle au développement de cette industrie tout en annonçant la création à venir d'une force dédiée. "J'annoncerai très prochainement la nomination d'un 'tsar' de l'IA", a-t-il ajouté.

france24fr.title: Mali: le bilan de l’attaque des jihadistes à Dioura s’alourdit à une centaine de militaires tués
france24fr.description: Au Mali, le bilan de l’attaque menée le 10 septembre 2026 par les jihadistes du Jnim, liés à al-Qaïda, contre le camp de l’armée à Dioura, dans la région de Mopti, s’alourdit. Selon plusieurs sources, au moins 100 militaires maliens ont été tués, soit deux fois plus que les premières estimations recueillies sur le terrain. Des dizaines d’autres soldats ont été faits prisonniers par les jihadistes.

france24fr.title: Festival Maillage : quelles voix pour raconter le monde d’aujourd’hui ?
france24fr.description:
Un nouveau festival littéraire voit le jour à Paris. Du 25 au 27 septembre 2026, Maillage investit le Palais de la Porte Dorée avec une ambition : faire circuler les récits et les formes, et donner à entendre une pluralité de voix autour des migrations, de l’exil, de la mémoire et des identités. Romans, poésie, bande dessinée, musique, performances et ateliers sont au programme de cette première édition, qui accueille Mohamed Mbougar Sarr comme invité d’honneur.

france24fr.title: France : le pass patrimoine, la nouveauté de cette rentrée 2026
france24fr.description: Grande nouveauté de la rentrée, le pass patrimoine a été mis en vente ce vendredi. Valentine Erba vous raconte son fonctionnement.

france24fr.title: Accès interdit à la Maison Blanche pour CNN, MS ​NOW et Politico
france24fr.description: Conformément ​à la décision annoncée la veille par le président américain Donald Trump, les ⁠journalistes de CNN, MS ​NOW et Politico ont été privés d'accès à la Maison blanche samedi. Les trois médias ont fait savoir que les accréditations depresse de leurs équipes avaient été ​confisquées lorsque leurs reporters se sont présentés devant la résidence du président américain.

france24fr.title: Arabie saoudite : flammes et fumée noire visibles près de l'aéroport de Ryad
france24fr.description: Des flammes et de la fumée noire sont apparues samedi 19 septembre près de l'aéroport de Ryad, où des explosions avaient retenti dans la nuit pour la première fois depuis la reprise des hostilités avec les Houthis du Yémen. "Il y a une escalade importante", analyse notre journaliste Antoine Mariotti.

france24fr.title: Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon : Macron et Carney veulent afficher "la souveraineté des nations"
france24fr.description: Un petit archipel français isolé mais stratégique aux confins de l'Atlantique Nord : Emmanuel Macron se rend de ce samedi 19 septembre à lundi 21 septembre à Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon, où il va afficher, au côté du Premier ministre Mark Carney, l'unité du Canada, de la France et des Européens et la "souveraineté des nations" face aux coups de boutoir de Donald Trump.

france24fr.title: Journées du patrimoine 2026 : mise en place d'un nouveau "Pass Patrimoine"
france24fr.description: À l'occasion des Journées européennes du patrimoine, les portes de monuments souvent fermés au public sont exceptionnellement ouvertes, et les visiteurs peuvent bénéficier d'une entrée gratuite. C'est le cas du musée Marmottan à Paris, où "certains visiteurs ont découvert sur place qu'ils n'auraient pas à payer", rapporte notre journaliste sur place Valentine Erba.

france24fr.title: Ligue 1 : le "clasico" pour l'OM et le PSG
france24fr.description: L'Olympique de Marseille reçoit le Paris Saint-Germain dimanche au Stade Vélodrome dans le cadre de la 5e journée de Ligue 1. Après avoir essuyé quatre défaites de suite – la dernière contre Beşiktaş (4-1) en Ligue Europa –, l'OM peut-il éviter la catastrophe ?

france24fr.title: Macron à Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon : "Une manière de rappeler la souveraineté française"
france24fr.description: Ce dimanche, Emmanuel Macron et le Premier ministre canadien Mark Carney doivent afficher la "souveraineté des nations" à Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon face à Donald Trump - qui publiait récemment encore une carte où la totalité de l'Amérique du Nord était affichée comme étasunienne... Pour le président français, "y passer trois jours est une manière de rappeler la souveraineté française", analyse notre invité Guillaume Poiret, géographe et spécialiste de l'Amérique du Nord.

france24fr.title: Russie : "Son armée piétine en Ukraine, alors elle accuse l'OTAN"
france24fr.description: La "nature de l’agressivité russe et des menaces en Europe changent", a prévenu le président de la République Emmanuel Macron ce 18 septembre. Nous en parlons avec notre invité Jacques Faure, ancien ambassadeur de France en Ukraine (2008-2011).

france24fr.title: Des bananes... made in Provence
france24fr.description:
La banane est le fruit le plus consommé des Français, c'est aussi le plus importé : 81% viennent d'Afrique, des Caraïbes et d'Amérique latine, parcourant des milliers de kilomètres avant d'arriver sur nos tables.
 
Et si, demain, elles poussaient à deux pas de chez vous ?
 
Dans le sud de la France, le dérèglement climatique redessine les cultures maraîchères. Plutôt que de lutter contre ce bouleversement, certains agriculteurs ont choisi de l'apprivoiser : ils se sont lancés dans la production

france24fr.title: La dette publique de la France frôlera les 122 % du PIB en 2027, un record
france24fr.description: Le ministère de l'Économie et des Finances a annoncé, samedi, que le niveau d'endettement de la France continuerait de se creuser pour atteindre les 119,3% du produit intérieur brut en 2026 et 121,7% en 2027.

france24fr.title: France Inter supprime l'édito contesté de Charles Sapin qui déplore "une censure préventive"
france24fr.description: Le journaliste Charles Sapin, directeur adjoint du magazine conservateur Valeurs actuelles, a annoncé, samedi, la "suppression" de son édito hebdomadaire sur France Inter. Le recrutement de ce journaliste avait déclenché un mouvement de protestation et une grève de deux jours, ses détracteurs dénonçant les idées d'extrême droite du journal. Charles Sapin leur a répondu sur son compte X.

france24fr.title: Arabie saoudite : des flammes visibles près de l'aéroport de Riyad après de fortes explosions
france24fr.description: Les habitants de la capitale saoudienne ont été réveillés dans la nuit de samedi à dimanche par une alerte de risque d'attaque suivie de deux fortes explosions. Le mouvement houthi au Yémen a revendiqué samedi une attaque contre des sites "sensibles" dans la capitale saoudienne, où des explosions avaient retenti dans la nuit pour la première fois depuis la reprise des hostilités entre Ryad et ces combattants pro-iraniens.

france24fr.title: Midterms 2026, le récap’ : les démocrates croient en la victoire, l'IA s’invite dans la campagne
france24fr.description: La dernière ligne droite de la campagne pour les Midterms a commencé ! Stratégie, candidats, sondages… Chaque semaine, France 24 fait le point sur ce qu'il faut retenir. Un sondage du New York Times publié mardi est venu conforter les espoirs des démocrates de remporter en novembre non seulement la Chambre des représentants mais aussi le Sénat. Et sur le terrain, les candidats s'emparent du thème brûlant de l'IA, notamment via la question des data centers.

france24fr.title: Michel Marx : "Dans mon enfance, tout dans l'organisation du quotidien était lié à la Shoah"
france24fr.description: Chaque semaine, Judith Grimaldi reçoit un invité dans son podcast "Avec Judith". L'invité de ce samedi est Michel Marx, scénariste et écrivain. Une partie de sa famille a péri dans la Shoah. Un héritage lourd qui a marqué son enfance : ses parents ne rentraient pas dans les détails, mais ce drame les suivait partout. Depuis des années, il tente de reconstituer le puzzle. Sa quête l'a mené à échanger avec Simone Veil et Ginette Kolinka, dont l'histoire est liée à celle de ses proches disparus.

nzz.title: Darüber spricht Nagoya: Will ich wirklich über 100 Jahre alt werden?
nzz.description: Nun könnte man in Japan eine ganze Stadt mit über 100-Jährigen füllen, 100 000 sind es mittlerweile. Japan ist stolz auf die Langlebigkeit seiner Bevölkerung und zelebriert das gesunde Leben. Allein, viele stellen sich auch die Frage, ob sie überhaupt so alt werden wollen.

nzz.title: Das US-Militär braucht seine Arsenale im Iran-Krieg auf. Daraus ergibt sich für Chinas Staatsführung eine historische Chance. Wird sie Peking nutzen?

nzz.title: London und sein Wexit – Die Preise in den Nobelvierteln sinken wegen des Exodus der Wohlhabenden. Und es könnte noch schlimmer kommen
nzz.description: «Wealth exit» oder kurz Wexit ist das neue Schlagwort in Grossbritannien. Zwar ist umstritten, wie viele Superreiche London verlassen haben. Allein im Immobilienmarkt hat deren Weggang deutliche Spuren hinterlassen. Ein Besuch im Nobelviertel Kensington.

nzz.title: Die Huthi in Jemen wollen mehr sein als nur die Handlanger Teherans
nzz.description: Mit der Kontrolle über die Meerenge Bab al-Mandab sind die Huthi zu einem Machtfaktor am Roten Meer geworden. Und ein Bündnis mit der Terrorgruppe in Somalia macht die Region rund um das Horn von Afrika noch unberechenbarer und gefährlicher für die Welt.

nzz.title: «Es ist der Beginn einer grossen Katastrophe» – Irans goldene Küsten färben sich schwarz

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Zum Glück war Frankenstein ein Schweizer

nzz.description: Eine Kooperation zwischen Kanada und der EU könnte auch für die Schweiz und Grossbritannien eine grosse Chance sein, findet der britische Publizist Gideon Rachman. Sorgen macht ihm die Gefährdung der Demokratie durch wirtschaftliche Stagnation, Ungleichheit und Social Media. Die Schweiz sei eine Ausnahme.

phys-org.description: Across Appalachia and the Rust Belt region, including throughout the city of Pittsburgh, former industrial sites are being transformed into new neighborhoods, research centers and technology hubs.

phys-org.title: How the malaria parasite boosts its transmission potential under stress conditions
phys-org.description: The malaria parasite is able to detect changes in its host's environment and respond by increasing the production of sexual forms capable of being transmitted to mosquitoes. A study led by the Barcelona Institute for Global Health (ISGlobal) identifies the molecular mechanism underlying this process. The findings, published in Nature Microbiology, answer what has been one of the major unanswered questions in malaria research for decades.

phys-org.title: Sacred springs of South Africa—pure waters or polluted? We found tiny bits of plastic in the samples we tested
phys-org.description: Across South Africa, natural springs are more than sources of freshwater. Some are places of healing, spiritual cleansing and rituals, where communities collect water and maintain longstanding cultural connections with the environment. For example, during cleansing rituals, people bathe in or collect spring water as a way of seeking spiritual renewal, healing and protection. These are known as sacred springs.

phys-org.title: Reconstructing the Great Miami Hurricane of 1926
phys-org.description: The first storm warning for the Miami area wasn't issued until only a few hours before the powerful cyclone made landfall just south of downtown, leaving residents with little time to prepare for what would become the hurricane of their nightmares.

phys-org.title: Two-color light steers electrons through graphene's transient topological state
phys-org.description: The electronic properties of materials are typically determined by their structure under normal, undisturbed conditions, when they are in a state known as equilibrium. Intense light beams, however, can temporarily reshape a material's electronic band structure (i.e., the range of energy states available to electrons), potentially giving rise to new electronic behaviors.

phys-org.title: A molecular bridge connects two signaling pathways critical for pollen development
phys-org.description: Cells rely on complex signaling networks in which different molecular pathways communicate with one another. Small GTPases act as molecular switches in these networks, controlling diverse cellular processes such as intracellular transport and cell morphogenesis. Although crosstalk between different families of small GTPases is established in animal cells, whether and how such crosstalk occurs in plants has remained largely unknown.

phys-org.title: Australia's vast Nullarbor Plain hides deep caves that can teach us about alien worlds
phys-org.description: Stretching more than 200,000 square kilometers (77,000 square miles) across southern Australia, the vast, flat plains of the Nullarbor mark one of the world's largest regions of limestone. It formed when an ancient shallow sea retreated some 14 million years ago.

phys-org.title: Bringing ice sheets to life: Releasing a dynamic ice sheet modeling workflow for Australia's climate model
phys-org.description: Ice sheets are fundamental components of the Earth system. Antarctica and Greenland, the two ice sheets currently on Earth, don't just affect their own regions: What happens on these vast masses of land ice influences weather, climate, society and the environment around the planet.

phys-org.title: Global population dataset uses buildings to reveal people's daily movement patterns
phys-org.description: Researchers at the Department of Energy's (DOE) Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL) have released LandScan Mosaic, a next-generation global population distribution dataset that estimates where people are by modeling how buildings are used and occupied throughout the day. Built on the foundation of ORNL's widely used LandScan Global, one of the world's most accurate population distribution datasets, Mosaic's enhancements will improve disaster response, humanitarian assistance

phys-org.title: How narwhal 'scientists' track Arctic warming
phys-org.description: The fight against climate change has a new, spiral-tusked ally: the narwhal.

phys-org.title: Meet Earth's newest wild cat species, the first named in over a century
phys-org.description: A previously unknown cat species has been identified in plain sight: at a wildlife sanctuary in Bolivia, where the small, spotted feline had been living for years.

phys-org.title: A humpback whale was spotted in a California river, 60 miles from its Pacific Ocean home
phys-org.description: Denny Glover was hoping for a big catch when he went fishing with buddies on the Sacramento River, but he wasn't expecting a fully grown humpback whale.

phys-org.title: The monsters that weren't: Dinosaur and tusked-beast claims in San rock art unravel
phys-org.description: For decades, an idea has grown in paleontology that, long before scientists began digging up and reconstructing dinosaur bones, the Indigenous San and Basotho in southern Africa noticed them too, incorporating them into songs, myths and immortalizing them on cave walls. But under closer scrutiny, these claims begin to crumble.

phys-org.title: Rethinking how we assess students could improve their well-being
phys-org.description: When you were in school, what stressed you out the most? For many students, classroom assessments—graded tests, quizzes, group work, presentations, labs and the like—would be near the top of the list.

phys-org.title: Florida scrub-jays attempt to breed at unusually young age after large-scale translocation
phys-org.description: For nearly two decades, biologist Lauren Deaner has worked with Florida scrub-jays, contributing to population recovery efforts and translocations. Now, as a doctoral researcher in UCF's integrative biology program, she is using that field experience to investigate how genetics, behavior and population dynamics influence the long-term recovery of imperiled species.

phys-org.title: Protein map reveals how red blood cells rapidly adjust to low oxygen
phys-org.description: Scientists map the hidden protein network that helps red blood cells adapt to oxygen

phys-org.title: Loss of Y chromosome in men could be an early warning sign of cancer
phys-org.description: A study initiated by Dr. Dan Theodorescu, a physician-scientist at the University of Arizona Cancer Center, revealed that the loss of the Y chromosome in men's body tissue could pave the way for cancer to develop. According to research recently published in JCI Insights, the loss of the chromosome, which is common in men as they age, creates a preneoplastic field effect, a hidden zone of genetic vulnerability in normal tissue that provides fertile ground for cancer to develop.

phys-org.title: Scientists simulate cosmic crashes to test whether icy moons gain or lose their ability to sustain life
phys-org.description: Many of the moons orbiting Saturn, Uranus and Neptune likely conceal oceans of liquid water beneath miles of icy shell. Because life as we know it needs water, these buried oceans rank among the most promising places to search for life beyond Earth.

undark.title: Review: A Vision of a Future Where Machines Fight Wars
undark.description: In “Lethal Autonomy,” Frank Kendall, a former top defense department official, envisions a military future where vehicles and weapons operate largely on their own — including making some decisions to strike people or infrastructure. And in his view, conflict is coming to space, making it all more urgent.

undark.title: Book Review: The Messy Business of Making Science Happen
undark.description: In “Lost in Curiosity: Field Notes From Scientists’ Adventures Into the Unknown,” Roberta Kwok sets out to smash the stereotype of eureka moments as the main drivers of scientific knowledge, largely by taking us inside the everyday world of science and scientists, in all its painstaking monotony.

undark.title: Book Review: Our Conflicted Relationship with the Sun
undark.description: Despite dermatological guidelines that decree sunlight a harmful carcinogen, Rowan Jacobsen argues in “In Defense of Sunlight” that the sun helps our skin produce many compounds vital to our health. How did science miss these benefits? The answer, he says, lies in our inability to do things in moderation.

undark.title: The New Student Visa Policy Doesn’t Add Up
undark.description: In July, the Department of Homeland Security issued new rules that would make it harder for international students to complete their studies in the U.S. The policy threatens to be disruptive for students — particularly doctoral candidates — and self-defeating for the country.

undark.title: Book Review: How Wildlife Is Returning to the East
undark.description: In “The Beasts of the East,” journalist Andrew Moore charts the natural history of the East and the people who have dedicated their careers to restoring several long lost species to what remains of their original habitats.

undark.title: Book Review: The Case for the AI-Powered Global Brain
undark.description: In “The God Test,” Robert Wright considers a future in which human consciousness becomes infused with AI. “We have to think seriously about a future in which there is something that increasingly resembles a global brain, and its neurons increasingly consist not just of human brains but of AIs,” he writes.

undark.title: Interview: How Tragedy Changed the FDA
undark.description: As an FDA advisory committee prepares to weigh whether specialized pharmacies should be allowed to dispense seven unapproved peptides, Mikkael A. Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?
undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

proj-syn.title: Africa’s AI Opportunity
proj-syn.description: The global AI revolution is often portrayed as a Sino-American race to develop the most advanced frontier models. But the greatest economic prize most likely will be found in deploying practical intelligence, particularly in Africa’s young, dynamic, and fast-growing economies.

proj-syn.title: The Political Earthquake From Germany’s China Shock
proj-syn.description: For decades, Germany’s stability rested on an implicit bargain: high-value manufacturing would provide good jobs, strong export revenues, and broad-based prosperity, which political institutions would translate into social cohesion. Competition from China shakes that bargain to its foundations.

proj-syn.title: Stopping the Far Right’s Rise
proj-syn.description: Leftists insist that what is behind the far right’s recent gains, from Europe to Central and South America, is economic precarity. Far-right leaders know better, winning elections or gaining support despite embracing very different economic policies.

proj-syn.title: Does Claude Have Rights?
proj-syn.description: Given the many differences between brains and LLMs, claiming that an AI is or might be conscious requires a high bar of evidence. But Anthropic’s constitution for Claude brushes that caveat aside, suggesting that we attribute sentience to non-biological beings.

proj-syn.title: A Congress for Europe’s Future
proj-syn.description: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen's recently proposed Congress of Europe is a step in the right direction, given the scale of Europe's geopolitical challenges. But to succeed, it must address the shortcomings that have hampered similar efforts in the past.

proj-syn.title: Can Adaptation Accelerate Climate Action?
proj-syn.description: After a summer of apocalyptic headlines, a new survey finds that people across the political spectrum are deeply concerned about preparing for the effects of global warming. The adaptation imperative may end up being the kind of crisis that forces us to stop neglecting the green agenda and act at the necessary scale.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s Iran Sanctions Have a China Problem
proj-syn.description: US President Donald Trump is trying to pressure the Iranian regime by isolating it from the dollar-based financial system. But because Iran’s oil trade largely moves through Chinese banks and renminbi-based networks, those sanctions increasingly depend on financial institutions beyond American control.

proj-syn.title: When AI Stops Asking Permission
proj-syn.description: The most useful lesson from this summer’s breach of Hugging Face by a swarm of OpenAI agents is about architecture, not intentions. AI agents need protective layers—limited access, separate authorization for sensitive actions, records nobody can quietly edit, and outside testing before deployment—not a lecture about good behavior.

proj-syn.title: Are Mexicans Really Better Off Under Claudia Sheinbaum?
proj-syn.description: For two consecutive years, Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum has pointed to reductions in extreme poverty to argue that Mexicans are better off today than they were in 2018. But a more holistic look at the available socioeconomic data casts doubt on that rosy picture.

proj-syn.title: The UN’s Credibility Test
proj-syn.description: Effective multilateralism depends on institutions that are transparent, accountable, and able to enforce their own rules. The United Nations should lead by example, from how it selects its next secretary-general to how it plans to ensure that governments follow through on their climate commitments.

proj-syn.title: A Workable Social Contract for the Climate Transition
proj-syn.description: Economic insecurity and growing distrust in institutions are undermining governments’ ability to sustain support for climate action. To rebuild that support, they must show that climate policies can reduce household bills, create decent jobs, and ensure that the biggest emitters pay their fair share.

proj-syn.title: It’s Time to Reconsider Inflation Targeting
proj-syn.description: Central banks were caught off guard by the inflationary surge of 2021–23 because they relied too heavily on inflation forecasts based on flawed models and ignored other warning signs. Their failure to recognize the rapid growth of the money supply, in particular, underscores the need to reassess their reliance on inflation targeting.

proj-syn.title: Democrats Need to Talk About Immigration
proj-syn.description: Radical right-wing parties have advanced across Western countries by successfully tying immigration to voters’ diffuse fears about their economic well-being, personal security, and cultural identity. Rather than ignoring or co-opting such claims, mainstream parties must offer equally robust counternarratives.

proj-syn.title: War in an Age of Weak Powers
proj-syn.description: The war in Iran has weakened both the United States and China, exposing the limits of their military power and strategic influence. Their troubles are creating a more dangerous geopolitical landscape while providing Europe with a rare opportunity to reform its governance model and reinvent its global role.

proj-syn.title: Hedging the AI Doomsday Risk
proj-syn.description: As far-fetched as warnings of an impending AI apocalypse may sound, even a remote risk should not be dismissed outright when human extinction is at stake. To guard against a danger of such extraordinary scale, governments and companies need to go beyond conventional risk-management strategies.

proj-syn.title: AI Is Only as Trustworthy as the Internet
proj-syn.description: Trust in technology is eroding at the very moment AI is putting more power in the hands of governments and Big Tech. Rebuilding that trust requires keeping the internet open and accessible so that new technologies can develop through broad participation rather than being shaped by the interests of a powerful few.

proj-syn.title: AI Demands Simpler Financial Regulation
proj-syn.description: AI could undermine financial oversight by giving market participants new ways to circumvent rules that regulators never anticipated. Overly complicated regulations give AI agents more ways to game the system, underscoring the need to streamline existing frameworks and equip officials with AI tools of their own.

proj-syn.title: The Strategic Asset Europe Has Overlooked
proj-syn.description: Europe’s soil is gradually dying, and yet the continent has still not recognized it as a strategic asset. Fortunately, the EU has many of the tools it needs to act, but doing so will require an overarching framework that helps farmers access financial rewards for measurable soil outcomes.

crunchbase.title: The Week’s 10 Biggest Funding Rounds: Large Rounds For AI Infrastructure, Space Tech And Investment Management Lead
crunchbase.description: After a week of multiple billion-dollar-plus rounds, startup investors have reduced the number of zeroes on their funding checks. This past week, the largest U.S. startup funding rounds were in the hundreds of millions, topped by a $550 million financing for AI infrastructure company Temporal Technologies and a $308 million investment in space vehicle developer Impulse Space.

crunchbase.title: What 25,000 Startup Applications Reveal About The New Rules Of Seed-Stage Startups
crunchbase.description: The most-fundable startups prioritize a clear go-to-market strategy and test distinctive marketing channels early, treating distribution and disciplined focus as durable competitive advantages, explains guest author Aaron Golbin, a co-founder and general partner at LvlUp Ventures, who believes that seed-stage success depends on focused execution, diversified financing, built-in distribution, rapid learning and AI designed as core infrastructure.
